phase_name: Authority Evaluation Model Implementation Contract Independent Re-Verification
summary: Phase 147F.1 independently re-verified AEMIC-001 v1.1. This phase independently reconstructed BF-147F-1 (Phase 147F, Blocking) directly from AEMIC-001 v1.1's own frozen text before re-reading either predecessor report's own account a second time, re-derived the minimum valid repaired evaluator interface, reassessed all five candidate repair families, verified the exact v1.0-to-v1.1 diff line by line, and attacked the repaired evaluate() signature, the citation_text if-and-only-if invariant (AEMIC-REQ-022/AEMIC-REQ-101), the disclosure-only security properties, and every carried-forward finding. Result: BF-147F-1 is confirmed fully and correctly repaired -- citation_text is reachable through evaluate()'s own fifth parameter, MissingCitationTextError closes the eligible-without-citation path, the invariant is satisfiable and satisfied on every path through the sole specified construction function for all three EvaluationResult values, EligibleAuthorityDeclaration's AEM-001-frozen six-field shape is untouched, and disclosure-only semantics are unweakened. However, this phase's own independent reconstruction discovered a second, distinct Blocking defect, BF-147F.1-1, missed by Phase 147C, Phase 147D, and Phase 147F: AuthorityEvaluationOutcome.template_ref and .template_version are mandatory output fields described as a verbatim copy of evaluate()'s own input, but evaluate()'s five-parameter signature never accepts template_ref or template_version as parameters; for the eligible/ineligible branches a value can be derived from declaration.template_ref/.template_version (undocumented, but at least available), while for the indeterminate branch (declaration is None) no value is reachable anywhere in evaluate()'s own inputs, so a mandatory output field cannot lawfully be constructed for a branch AEM-REQ-017/AEMIC-REQ-024 require evaluate() to support. This defect predates the citation-text repair, is untouched by it, and is unrelated to it. Three narrow Non-Blocking observations were also newly disclosed (empty-string citation_text is not distinguished from a valid one; non-string citation_text typing is not explicitly named as a raising condition; from_payload's own cross-field validation for conditionally-mandatory fields is ambiguous), plus one Informational note (direct AuthorityEvaluationOutcome construction bypassing evaluate() is not formally forbidden by any binding requirement, though the type remains non-authoritative by design, mirroring AEM-001's own no-enforcement-surface reasoning). F-147C-1 is now independently confirmed fully reconciled (both at the textual-source level and, now that BF-147F-1 is repaired, at the plumbing level); F-147C-2, FA-147D-1, FA-147D-2, FA-147D-3, F-147F-2, and F-147F-3 were each independently re-derived from primary sources and reconfirmed with their existing disposition, unaffected by this repair. Overall Verdict: REPAIR NOT VERIFIED (for AEMIC-001 v1.1 taken as a whole; BF-147F-1 itself is independently confirmed Repaired). Full detail in docs/PHASE_147F.1_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_MODEL_IMPLEMENTATION_CONTRACT_INDEPENDENT_REVERIFICATION.md. Canonical finalization for this phase was not completed in the original working session (the substantive verification document was produced and validated, but pcae phase complete, the completion-metadata sync, the commit, the push, and the terminal notification were never invoked before the session ended); Phase 147F.1R (Canonical Report and Finalization Recovery) subsequently recovered this metadata, PROJECT_STATUS.md's Current Phase section, task-lifecycle bookkeeping, and the finalization commit/push/notification without altering any substantive Phase 147F.1 finding, verdict, or recommendation. Full detail of the recovery itself is in docs/PHASE_147F.1R_CANONICAL_REPORT_AND_FINALIZATION_RECOVERY.md.
